en: Now begins the eighty-first chapter: The Chapter on the Results of the Characteristics of the Limbs.
O Sage, you have described in many ways the auspicious and inauspicious [results] from the time of birth;
now I wish to hear, O Sage, the results [indicated] by the bodily marks of women.
Listen, O Brahmin, I shall declare the inauspicious characteristics of women, just as the Blessed Lord Śaṅkara spoke them to Pārvatī. (2)
The soles of women's feet that are glossy, soft, fleshy, even, red, free from perspiration, and warm bestow great enjoyment. (3)
A mark that is discolored, rough, broken, uneven, shaped like a winnowing basket, or dry, bestows suffering and misfortune. || 4 ||
She whose soles bear the marks of a conch, a svastika, a wheel, a lotus, a banner, a fish, and a parasol is to be known as the consort of a king.
Likewise, a long, vertical line leads to the enjoyment of all pleasures;
lines resembling a serpent, a mouse, or a crow indicate suffering and poverty.
Red, elevated, glossy, and rounded toenails are auspicious;
those that are cracked or black in color should be known as indicators of inauspiciousness. || 7 ||
A thumb that is elevated, fleshy, and round bestows incomparable enjoyments;
one that is crooked, short, and flattened indicates suffering and poverty. || 8 ||
Fingers that are soft, thick, rounded, and fleshy are praised;
with long fingers one becomes unchaste, and with thin ones, destitute of wealth.
If the lines are short, she will have a short life; if they are uneven, she will be a procuress; if they are flat, she will be a servant; and if they are sparse, she will be destitute.
For she whose toes are intertwined with one another shall indeed become a servant to others, even after abandoning many husbands.
That woman whose dust rises from the earth as she walks along the path is a "dusty" woman (pāṃsulī), who brings ruin to three lineages.
She whose little toe does not touch the ground as she walks will indeed kill her first husband and take a second one. (13)
O best of the twice-born, that woman whose middle and ring fingers do not touch the ground should be known as one who is deprived of a husband.
If her ring finger extends beyond the thumb, she is considered a defiled maiden; moreover, she will become an unchaste woman. (15)
If the instep of the foot is elevated, then she will certainly be a queen;
it should be free from perspiration, devoid of prominent veins, fleshy, smooth, and soft. (16)
Otherwise, if it is devoid of flesh, she is poor; if it is veiny, she is a traveler;
if it is hairy, she is a slave; and if it is fleshless, she is unfortunate. (17)
A woman with even heels is fortunate; one with broad heels is unfortunate;
one with high heels is unchaste; and one with long heels is miserable. (18)
She whose shanks are symmetrical, smooth, well-rounded, free from veins, and beautiful will certainly become the wife of a king. (19)
A pair of knees that are rounded, fleshy, and smooth bestows auspiciousness;
those that are fleshless belong to a woman who acts according to her own will, and those that are loose belong to a woman who is destitute.
She whose thighs are thick, shaped like an elephant's trunk, rounded, soft, auspicious, and free of visible veins, will certainly become a queen. (21)
She whose buttocks are flattened and hairy is a widow and ill-fated; however,
a waist that is even with forty-four finger-breadths (aṅgulas) and endowed with well-elevated hips is praised for women with eyes like those of a deer.
A waist that is sunken, flat, long, fleshless, and narrow, being short and covered with hair, indicates suffering and widowhood. (23)
A navel that is deep, elevated, fleshy, and broad is said to bestow auspiciousness upon women and grant happiness and good fortune; otherwise, it should be known as a bringer of misery. (24)

For women, the vulva is auspicious when it has hidden jewels, is elevated, reddish in hue, covered with soft hair, resembles the back of a tortoise, and has the shape of a branch of the holy fig tree (aśvattha). || 25 ||
One who has the form of a deer's hoof, whose belly resembles the interior of a cooking pot,
who is hairy, has a visible nose, and has a wide-open mouth, brings misfortune.
A girl born from the left side is elevated, while one born from the right side is a boy;
she whose vulva is coiled like a conch shell is considered a woman who will not conceive.
A soft vulva is praised if it is broad, slightly elevated, and rich in hair; however, one that is veiny and marked with lines does not bestow auspiciousness. (28)
A navel that is deep, spiraling to the right, and bestowing all happiness is auspicious;
one with clearly defined folds, level, and spiraling to the left is not beautiful. (29)
A woman with a broad belly gives birth to many sons;
she who has a belly resembling a frog shall give birth to a son who becomes a lord of the earth.
A woman whose abdomen is protruding, wrinkled, and marked with whirlpools will be born respectively as a barren woman, a female renunciant, or a slave. (31)
The sides of women that are even, symmetrical, soft, and elevated are auspicious;
those that are hairy and veiny are inauspicious.
A woman’s heart that is free from greed and even is the bestower of all happiness; one that is broad and hairy should be known as the bestower of inauspiciousness. || 33 ||
For women, breasts that are symmetrical, full, firm, rounded, and solid are praised; those with thick tips, sparse nipples, or that are shriveled do not bring auspiciousness at all. (34)
A woman whose right breast is elevated is considered to have sons;
one whose left breast is elevated is said by the ancients to have daughters as offspring. (35)
For women, nipples that are dark-colored and well-rounded are auspicious;
however, those that are sunken inward, elongated, or thin are not beautiful.

For women, shoulders that are symmetrical, well-developed, and with hidden joints bestow auspiciousness; those that are excessively hairy, elevated, crooked, or fleshless are considered inauspicious. (37)
In women, the armpits that have very fine hair, are well-nourished, smooth, and glossy bring auspiciousness; those that are veiny, deep-set, and covered with sweat and fat are not auspicious.
The arms of deer-eyed women are praised when they have hidden bones, soft joints, no prominent veins, and no body hair; they should be straight and well-rounded. (39)
The arms of women that are fleshless, with thick hair, short, and covered with visible veins, as well as those that are crooked, are proclaimed to lead to suffering. (40)
The thumbs of deer-eyed women that have the shape of lotus buds are said to bestow all happiness; those that are thin and crooked bring suffering. (41)
The palms of women should be known as red, with a raised center, free from cracks, soft, and marked with few lines; such hands bestow all happiness.
Indeed, by her palm having many lines, a woman becomes a widow; by being devoid of lines, she is destitute; and by having a head-like mark on the palm, she becomes a beggar. (43)
The back of the hand of women that is auspicious is well-nourished, soft, and hairless;
one that is veiny, hairy, or depressed indicates suffering and poverty. (44)
She on whose palm the lines are distinct, red, circular, glossy, full, and deep, shall be a partaker of all happiness. (45)

One with a fish [mark] is to be known as fortunate; one with a svastika is endowed with wealth; one with a lotus becomes the wife of a king; and one with a lotus becomes the mother of a lord of the earth. (46)
One who has a river-curl on her hand turning clockwise will become the beloved of a sovereign ruler;
one with the marks of a conch, a parasol, and a tortoise will become the mother of a king.
She who has a line on her hand shaped like a balance is indeed the wife of a merchant;
or, if there are lines resembling an elephant, a horse, or a bull on the left hand of that deer-eyed woman, [she is likewise]. (48)
A line with the luster of a clear diamond produces a son who is a Tīrthaṅkara; a line shaped like a plowshare or a yoke indicates she will be the wife of a farmer. (49)
The king’s devoted wife was marked with lines in the shape of chowries, goads, and bows; she bore the forms of tridents, swords, maces, spears, and drums.
If a line emerging from the base of the thumb extends to the little finger, that woman will be a slayer of her husband; one should avoid her from afar.
Lines resembling a crow, a frog, a jackal, a wolf, a scorpion, a serpent, a donkey, a camel, or a cat bring suffering to a woman. (52)
The fingers of women are declared auspicious when they are soft, well-jointed, long, rounded, gradually tapering, and hairless. (53)
Those that are too short, thin, crooked, sparse, covered with hair, or possessing too many joints, as well as those lacking joints, cause suffering. (54)
Nails that are red in color, elevated, and possessed of a crest (shikhā) bestow auspiciousness;
those that are sunken, discolored, yellow, or spotted bring about suffering. || 55 ||
A back with the spinal vertebrae submerged within it and well-fleshed is auspicious;
however, one that is covered in hair up to the head or is crooked brings inauspiciousness. || 56 ||
In women, a neck marked with three lines, having indistinct bones, being circular, fleshy, and soft, bestows auspicious results. (57)
A woman with a thick neck becomes a widow, one with a crooked neck a servant, one with a flat neck is barren, and one with a short neck is childless. || 58 ||
The nape of the neck is excellent when it is straight, fleshy, and well-elevated;
it is inauspicious when it is withered, veiny, hairy, broad, or crooked. (59)
A woman's chin that is ruddy, soft, well-filled, and prominent is praiseworthy;
one that is long, hairy, thick, or divided into two parts is inauspicious.
In women, cheeks that are elevated, full, and rounded bestow auspiciousness;
those that are hairy, sunken, and fleshless in men bring inauspiciousness. (61)
The face of women that is even, the back that is rounded and fragrant, and that which is very glossy and captivating, indicates happiness and good fortune. (62)
She whose lower lip is rounded, pale-red, and whose center is adorned with glossy lines, being truly captivating, shall become the beloved of kings. (63)
If the lower lip of women is fleshless, cracked, hanging, dry, or dark-colored, and if it is thick, it indicates the suffering of widowhood.
The upper lip of deer-eyed women that resembles a red lotus, is glossy, slightly elevated in the middle, and hairless, brings about happiness and good fortune. (65)
The thirty-two teeth of women are auspicious when they resemble glossy honey;
they are even above and below, and slightly elevated.
Teeth that are larger at the bottom, yellow, dark, long, arranged in two rows, protruding, or widely spaced are considered inauspicious. (67)
A tongue that is reddish, soft, and beautiful bestows incomparable enjoyment upon women;
one that is of medium size, variegated, and very broad at the tip brings suffering. (68)
With a white [line], there is death in water; with a dark one, she is fond of quarrels;
with a fleshy one, she is destitute of wealth; and with a hanging one, she is an eater of forbidden food. (69)
A woman accompanied by negligence has a broad tongue;
the palate of women is very smooth, pale-red, soft, and beautiful. (70)
If the palate is white, there will be widowhood; if yellow, she will become a renunciant;
if black, she will be childless; and if dry, she will have a large family.
The smile of women, in which the teeth are not visible and the cheeks are slightly blooming, should be known as bestowing auspiciousness; otherwise, it bestows inauspiciousness. (72)
A nose with even nostrils and small openings bestows auspiciousness;
however, one that is thick at the tip or depressed in the middle is not praised for women with deer-like eyes.
A nose with a red tip or one with a curved tip brings widowhood; she whose nose is flat becomes a servant, and she whose it is short or long is fond of strife.
The auspicious eyes of women have reddish corners and black pupils;
they are white like the color of cow’s milk, very clear, exceedingly lustrous, and possess black eyelashes.
A woman with protruding eyes does not have a long life, while one with round eyes becomes unchaste;
a woman with honey-brown eyes shall be a partaker of happiness and good fortune. (76)
A woman who is squint-eyed in the left eye is unchaste; one who is squint-eyed in the right is barren;
one with eyes like a pigeon’s is of bad character; and one with eyes like an elephant’s is not auspicious at all. (77)
A woman with eyelashes that are soft, black, thick, and fine is endowed with good fortune;
one with eyelashes that are sparse, reddish-brown, and coarse is a partaker of suffering.
The eyebrows of beautiful women, when they are circular, bow-shaped, glossy, black, unjoined, and possessed of soft hair, bestow happiness and fame. (79)
Ears that are long and possess auspicious curls bestow sons and good fortune; those lacking the ear-lobes, or which are veiny, crooked, or thin, are censurable. (80)
A forehead free from prominent veins, hairless, radiant like the half-moon, and measuring three finger-breadths in depth, bestows sons, good fortune, and happiness upon women. (81)
A forehead marked with a clearly defined svastika bestows sovereignty upon a woman;
one that is overly long, hairy, or excessively high is said to bring suffering.
A woman’s head that is elevated, rounded like an elephant’s frontal globe, and auspicious brings prosperity;
however, one that is thick, long, or crooked indicates suffering and misfortune. (83)
Tresses that are soft, black, fine, long, and beautiful are auspicious;
those that are tawny, coarse, sparse, and short are inauspicious for men. (84)
For a woman of fair complexion, reddish-brown lines are auspicious; for one of dark complexion, they should be dark.
One should consider these characteristics of women, and likewise those of men as well. (85)
Now begins the chapter on the results of branding with sesame seeds and other substances. 82.
Now I shall declare the fruit of the marks born upon the body—specifically of the whirlpools, the sesame seeds, and the moles. || 1 ||
For women, on the left side, and for men, on the right side,
there is auspiciousness if there is a mark resembling a red glow, a tilaka, or even a circle of hair.
A sesame seed or other mark upon the hearts of women is an indicator of good fortune;
she who has a red sesame seed or mark on her right breast [is likewise blessed].
She gives birth to a lineage endowed with happiness and good fortune;
for that woman on whose left breast there is a red-tinged mole (tilaka), [she shall have such offspring]. (4)
Those who know the truth understand that she has only one son;
however, if there is a *tilaka* on her right breast, she should be known as having both a daughter and a son.
A mole between the eyebrows or on the forehead indicates a passionate nature;
a red freckle on the cheek constantly bestows sweet foods.
If a woman has a mole on the right side of her hip,
she will indeed be the wife of a lord of the earth or will give birth to a son who becomes a king.
If a red mark appears at the tip of the nose of a king’s wife, she will give birth [to a son];
however, she whose mark is black in color is either an unchaste woman or a widow.
A mark below the navel in men, or on the ear, the cheek, the hand, or the throat in women, bestows auspiciousness. (9)
O Brahmin, a mark on the ankle that bestows a son in the womb beforehand, as well as happiness and good fortune, is known to be auspicious; however, if it is located on the heel, it brings suffering.
If a mark in the shape of a trident appears on the forehead, the woman should be known as a favorite of the king, and the man shall become a lord of the earth. || 11 ||
The clockwise whorl of body hair on the chest, navel, hand, ear, right back, or the auspicious bladder region brings good fortune; a counter-clockwise whorl is a giver of inauspiciousness.
A whorl on the hip or in the private parts indicates misfortune for women;
one on the abdomen kills the husband, and one on the middle of the back marks a woman of loose character.
O best of the twice-born, a whorl (āvarta) on the throat, forehead, hairline, the middle part, or the crown of the head is not auspicious for women or even for men.
Even women who possess auspicious marks and virtuous conduct can, through their influence, cause a husband of short life to become long-lived and a source of joy. (15)
Now begins the chapter on the manifestation of curses from previous births, the eighty-third.
O Great Sage, you have described the fruits for women and men separately;
now, O best among the knowers of the Vedas, I wish to hear from you [further].
"O Sage, it is heard in the scriptures that there is no destination for one who is sonless;
tell me, O Lord, by what sin does one become sonless? (2)
How can that knowledge [of the future] regarding the birth-ascendant be obtained by those who know destiny?
Out of compassion, please tell me the means for a sonless man to obtain a son. (3)
Well asked by you, O Brahmin;
indeed, it shall be told by me just as it was formerly related by Śiva when he was questioned by Umā.
By what sinful yoga is the destruction of offspring known to occur?
O Lord, please tell me out of compassion the means for their protection. (5)
"Excellent, O Goddess, you have asked well; I shall now tell you of the astrological yogas that cause the loss of progeny, along with the means for their protection."
When the lord of the ascendant, the lord of the seventh house,
and the lords of the fifth and ninth houses are all devoid of strength, childlessness must be predicted.

If the Sun, Mars, Rāhu, and Saturn are strong and situated in the fifth house, then there will be childlessness; however, if they are weak, the significators of children (putrakārakas) may produce offspring.
If Rāhu is situated in the fifth house and aspected by Mars,
or if it has entered the sign of Mars, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a serpent.

If Rāhu is conjoined with Saturn in the fifth house, or if Venus is situated in the fifth house and conjoined with or aspected by the Moon, there will be the loss of sons due to the curse of a serpent.

If Rāhu is conjoined with a Karaka planet, the lord of the fifth house is devoid of strength, and the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with Mars, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a serpent. || 11 ||

If Mars is conjoined with the ascendant and Rāhu is also conjoined with the ascendant, and the lord of the fifth house is situated in an inauspicious house, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a serpent. || 12 ||
If the ninth house is a portion of Mars and is conjoined with Mars, and the lord of the fifth house is the Moon or Jupiter,
yet is joined with Rāhu and Māndi in the ascendant, there is loss of children due to the curse of a serpent.
If Mars occupies the fifth house and the lord of the fifth is conjoined with Rāhu,
even if it is aspected by or conjoined with benefics, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a serpent.
Bhānu, Mandāra, Svabhānu, Śaśija, and Aṅgirā occupy the fifth house;
if the lord of the fifth house and the lord of the ascendant are both weak due to the curse of the serpent, there is the loss of children. (15)

If the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with Rāhu, the lord of the fifth house is conjoined with Mars, or the Karaka is conjoined with Rāhu, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a serpent. || 16 ||
Having thus understood the childlessness of men through the influence of planetary conjunctions, one should undertake the worship of the Nāgas for the purpose of removing that defect. (17)
The wise person should perform the consecration according to the ritual procedure prescribed in his own *gṛhya-sūtra*.
Having fashioned an image of the Naga out of gold, he should carry out the worship. (18)
One should give cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, and so forth, according to one's wealth;
for when this is done, the lineage prospers through the grace of the Lord of Nagas.
When the Sun has entered the fifth house (the house of children), being debilitated and situated in its own Navamsha,
and when there is an association with malefic planets on both sides, there is the destruction of children due to the curse of the ancestors.

If the Sun, the lord of the fifth house, is in a trine and conjoined with malefic planets, or situated between malefics and aspected by malefics, there is loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors. || 21 ||
When Jupiter is situated in the sign of the Sun and the lord of the fifth house is conjoined with the Sun,
and the fifth house or the ascendant is filled with malefic planets, there is a loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors.

If the lord of the ascendant is weak, or if the lord of the fifth house is conjoined with the Sun, or if the fifth house is in the ascendant and conjoined with malefic planets, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors. || 23 ||

If the lord of the fourth house is in the fifth house, or if the lord of the fifth house is in the tenth house, and the fifth house or the ascendant is occupied by malefic planets, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors. (24)
If Mars, the lord of the eighth house, is conjoined with the lord of the fifth house,
and there are malefics in the ascendant, the fifth, or the eighth house, there will be the destruction of progeny.
If the lord of the fifth house is in an unfavorable position, the significator (kāraka) is in a malefic sign,
and both the lord of the fifth house and the lord of the ascendant are associated with malefics, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors.

If the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are situated in the ascendant and the fifth house, while Rāhu and Jupiter are in the eighth or twelfth house, there is loss of children due to the curse of one's ancestors. (27)

If the Sun is in the eighth house from the ascendant, Saturn is in the fifth house, the lord of the fifth house is conjoined with Rāhu, and there is a malefic in the ascendant, there will be the loss of children. || 28 ||

If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the ascendant, the lord of the eighth house is in the fifth house, and the lord of the fourth house is in the eighth house, there is a loss of children due to the father's curse. || 29 ||
When the lord of the ninth house is situated in the fifth house, the lord of the fourth house is in the sixth house,
and the significator is conjoined with Rāhu, there is loss of children due to the curse of the ancestors.
To avoid those defects, one should perform a śrāddha at Gayā and feed ten thousand or a thousand Brahmins there.
Alternatively, one should perform the gift of a maiden and the gift of a cow;
when this is done, one is liberated from the father's curse—of this there is no doubt. (32)
And his lineage always flourishes through sons, grandsons, and so forth;
thus, the wise astrologer should declare the results according to the conjunctions of the planets. || 33 ||
If the Moon, the lord of the fifth house, is in its sign of debilitation or situated between malefic planets,
and if malefics are in the fourth and fifth houses, there will be loss of children due to the mother's curse.

If Saturn is conjoined with [malefics] in the house of gain (the eleventh), and there is an inauspicious planet in the mother's place (the fourth), and the Moon is in its sign of debilitation in the fifth house, there is loss of children due to the curse of the mother. || 35 ||
If the lord of the fifth house is in an unfavorable position, the lord of the ascendant is in its sign of debilitation,
and the Moon is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be loss of children due to the mother's curse.

If the Moon is situated in the eighth, sixth, or twelfth house from the lord of the fifth house, and is conjoined with a malefic’s portion, and if both the ascendant and the fifth house are occupied by malefics, there will be a loss of children due to the mother’s curse. || 37 ||
If the Moon, the lord of the fifth house,
is conjoined with Mars, there will be a loss of children due to the mother's curse, whether in the ninth house or the fifth house.
If Mars, the lord of the fifth house from the mother's position, is conjoined with Saturn and Rāhu,
or joined by the Moon and the Sun in the fifth house or in the ascendant, there will be a decline in progeny.

If the lords of the ascendant and the fifth house are situated in the sixth house, and the lord of the fourth house is situated in the eighth house, there is destruction of the son due to the father's death and the mother's curse. (40)

If the lords of the sixth and eighth houses are situated in the ascendant, and the lord of the fourth house is in the twelfth while the Moon and Jupiter are joined with malefic planets, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of the mother. (41)
If the ascendant is situated in a malefic sign and the Moon is waned (kṣīṇa) in the seventh house,
and Rāhu and Saturn are in the fifth house, there is loss of children due to the mother's curse.

If the lord of the eighth house is in the fifth house, the lord of the fifth house is in the eighth house, and the lord of the fourth house is in an inauspicious house, there is loss of children due to the curse of the mother. (43)
When the ascendant is in the sign of Cancer and is occupied by Mars and Rāhu, with the Moon and Saturn situated in the fifth house, there is a loss of sons due to the curse of the mother. (44)
If Mars, Rāhu, the Sun, and Saturn are situated in the ascendant, the fifth, the eighth, and the twelfth houses respectively,
and the lord of the mother’s sign and the lord of the ascendant are in malefic positions, there is loss of children due to the curse of the mother.

When Jupiter has gone to the house of destruction (the eighth house) conjoined with Mars and Rāhu, and Saturn and the Moon are in the house of sons (the fifth house), there is the loss of children due to the mother's curse. (46)
Having observed such a conjunction, the wise should recognize the prospect of childlessness;
therefore, for the sake of protecting the lineage, the highest propitiatory rite (śānti) must be performed. || 47 ||
One should perform the ritual bath at Setu while reciting the Gāyatrī mantra one hundred thousand times;
having drunk a measure of milk from silver, one should diligently perform the gift for the planets (grahadāna).
In that same manner, one should feed Brahmins; furthermore, one who is filled with devotion should perform the circumambulation of the Aśvattha tree one thousand and eight times.
O Great Goddess, when this is done, there will be liberation from the curse;
thereafter, one obtains a virtuous son and the prosperity of the lineage arises. (50)
Now, moreover, I shall declare the yogas arising from the curse of the brothers;
knowing which, a wise man should exert effort for the sake of protecting his offspring. (51)

If the lord of the fifth house occupies the position of the lord of the third house and is conjoined with Mars and Rāhu, and both the lord of the fifth house and the lord of the ascendant are in the eighth house, there is destruction of children due to the curse of a brother. 52.
If Mars and Saturn are in the ascendant and the fifth house, and the lord of the third house is in the ninth house,
while the significator (the Sun) is situated in the eighth house, there is loss of children due to the curse of a brother.

If Jupiter is in the debilitation sign in the house of brothers, or Saturn is situated in the fifth house, or if the Moon and Mars are in the eighth house, there is destruction of children due to the curse of a brother. (54)
If Mars is in the eighth house while the lord of the second house is in the twelfth,
and the lord of the fifth house is in the eighth along with a malefic, there will be loss of children due to the curse of a brother.
If the ascendant is situated between malefics and the fifth house is likewise between malefics,
and the lords of the ascendant and the fifth house are in weak houses, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a brother.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the third house and is joined with a malefic as well as a benefic,
or if it is conjoined with Mars in the fifth house, there is a loss of children due to the curse of a brother.

If the fifth house is a sign of Mercury and is conjoined with Saturn and Rāhu, and the twelfth house is afflicted by Mars and Rāhu, one should know that there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a brother. 58.
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the third house, the lord of the third house is in the fifth house,
and malefic planets occupy the ascendant, the third, and the fifth houses, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a brother.
If the lord of the third house is situated in the eighth house and the Karaka is likewise in the fifth house,
conjoined with or aspected by Rahu and Saturn, there is loss of children due to the curse of a brother.
If the lord of the eighth house is in the fifth house conjoined with the lord of the third house,
and Mars and Saturn are conjoined in the eighth house, there is destruction of children due to the curse of a brother.
For the sake of liberation from his brother’s curse, he should listen to the lineage of Hari;
thereafter, he should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance in the presence of Viṣṇu at the Kāverī.
One should perform the installation of the Aśvattha tree and cause ten cows to be given as gifts;
with the hand of his wife, the son should offer land endowed with fruit.
Thus, for one who performs this with devotion, accompanied by his lawful wife, a son will certainly be born and the increase of the lineage will come to pass. (64)

If Mercury or Jupiter occupies the house of the son (the fifth house) while being conjoined with Mars and Rāhu, and Saturn is in the ascendant, the fifth house should be understood as representing the maternal uncle due to his curse. || 65 ||
If the lords of the ascendant and the fifth house are conjoined with Mercury, Mars, and Saturn in the fifth house,
one should know that there will be a decline in progeny for the person due to the curse of a maternal uncle.

If the lord of the fifth house is absent from the ascendant and the Sun’s son (Saturn) is in the seventh house, and the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with Mercury, there will also be a destruction of his progeny. || 67 ||
If the lord of the fourth house is in the ascendant conjoined with the lord of the twelfth house,
and the Moon, Mercury, and Mars are in the fifth house, a decline in progeny is to be known.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the worship of Viṣṇu and undertake the digging of ponds, wells, tanks, and so forth, which brings blessings from one's sons and kinsmen. (69)
"An increase in sons will come to him, and an increase in prosperity arises.
Thus, by the power of yoga, the wise man should perform this rite of pacification.
That mortal who, out of pride in his strength, treats Brahmins with contempt, shall suffer the destruction of his lineage due to that fault and the curse of the Brahmins. (71)
When Rāhu is in the ninth house (guru-kṣetra), and Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn are in the fifth house,
and the lord of the ninth house is in the eighth house, there is loss of children due to the curse of a Brahmin.
When the lord of the ninth house is situated in the fifth house, and the lord of the fifth house is in the eighth house,
conjoined with Jupiter, Mars, and Rahu, there is the destruction of children due to the curse of a Brahmin.

If the lord of the ninth house is debilitated and the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the fifth house, conjoined with or aspected by Rāhu, there is destruction of children due to the curse of a Brahmin. || 74 ||

If Rāhu is in its sign of debilitation, or in the ascendant, or in the fifth house, and the lord of the fifth house is situated in an inauspicious house, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a Brahmin. (75)

If Jupiter, the lord of the fifth house, is in the eighth house conjoined with malefic planets, or if the lord of the fifth house is with the Sun and Moon, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a Brahmin. (76)
When Jupiter is in its debilitated portion, conjoined with Saturn,
and associated with Mars, and the lord of the fifth house is situated in the twelfth house, there is a loss of children due to the curse of Brahmā.
If Jupiter is conjoined with Saturn in the ascendant, while Rāhu is situated in the ninth house,
or if Jupiter is conjoined with [Saturn] in the twelfth house, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of a Brahmin.
To pacify that fault, a man should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance;
having performed the Brahmakūrca rite three times, he should give a bow along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
The five jewels, together with gold, should be given;
thereafter, O best of the twice-born, one should feed the Brahmins according to one's ability. (80)
When this is done, one obtains a virtuous son; of this there is no doubt.
Freed from the curse and purified in soul, that man prospers in happiness.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the fifth house and Saturn is the ruler of the navāṃśa of the lord of the seventh,
and the lord of the fifth house is in a sign of destruction (the eighth), there is loss of children due to the curse of the wife.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the eighth house, and the lord of the fifth house is in the eighth house,
and the significator (Kāraka) is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of the wife.
When Venus is situated in the house of the son (the fifth), Mars is in the eighth house,
and the significator (the lord of the fifth) is conjoined with malefic planets, there is a loss of children due to the curse of the wife.
When the Moon is in the house of destruction (the eighth) in a family associated with evil, and the son is joined by malefic planets, there is the loss of children due to the curse of the wife. (85)
When Venus is situated in the house of fortune (the second house) and the lord of the seventh house is in the house of destruction (the eighth house),
and both the ascendant and the fifth house are heavily afflicted by malefic planets, there is a loss of children due to the curse of the wife.

If Venus, the lord of the ninth house, is in the sign of an enemy to the lord of the fifth house, and Jupiter, the lord of the ascendant, and the lord of the seventh house are in malefic houses, there will be a decline in progeny. (87)
If Bhṛgukṣetra (Venus) is in the fifth house conjoined with Rāhu and the Moon,
and malefic planets are in the twelfth, ascendant, and second houses, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of one's wife.

If Saturn and Venus are in the seventh house, the lord of the eighth is in the fifth house, and the Sun is in the fifth, while Rahu is conjoined with the Ascendant, there is a loss of children due to the curse of one's wife. (89)
If Mars is in the second house, Jupiter in the twelfth, and Venus in the fifth house,
conjoined with or aspected by Saturn and Rāhu, there is the loss of children due to the curse of one's wife.
If the lords of the second and seventh houses are situated in the eighth house, and Mars and Saturn are in the fifth house or the ascendant,
while the significator (Kāraka) is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be the loss of children due to the curse of the wife.
If Rāhu, Saturn, and Mars are situated respectively in the ascendant, the fifth house, and the ninth house;
and the lords of the fifth and seventh houses are both located in the eighth house, there is loss of children due to the curse of the wife. (92)
For the sake of liberation from the curse, one should perform that gift when a daughter is present;
and in the absence of a daughter, [one should give] an image of Śrī Viṣṇu accompanied by Lakṣmī.
O Brahmin, one should give a golden bed accompanied by ten cows,
along with ornaments and clothing for the couple among the twice-born.
Surely he shall have a son, and an increase in fortune arises for him;
however, if there is a lapse in the rites for the ancestors, his state becomes that of a preta.
And due to the curse of that deceased person, the absence of a son is produced;
therefore, I shall here explain such [planetary] configurations from the birth ascendant. (96)
If Saturn and the Sun occupy the fifth house, the Moon is waning,
Rāhu and Jupiter are in the ascendant and the twelfth house, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.
If Saturn is the lord of the fifth house and is situated in the eighth, Mars is in the ascendant, and the significator (Jupiter) is in the eighth house,
there is a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.
If a malefic is in the ascendant, the Sun is in the twelfth house, and Mercury, Saturn, and the Moon are in the fifth house,
while the lord of the fifth house is situated in the eighth house, there will be a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.
When the Ascendant is conjoined with Rāhu, Saturn is situated in the fifth house,
and Jupiter is in a sign of destruction (Nāśarāśi), there is a loss of sons due to the curse of a ghost.
If Rāhu is in the ascendant along with Venus and Jupiter, and the Moon is conjoined with Saturn;
and if the lord of the ascendant is situated in the house of death (the eighth house), there is a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost. || 101 ||
If the lord of the fifth house is in its sign of debilitation, the significator (Kāraka) is in its sign of debilitation,
and it is aspected by a planet situated in its sign of debilitation, there is loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.
If Saturn is in the ascendant, Rāhu in the fifth house, the Sun in the eighth house,
and Mars is conjoined with [the Moon] in the twelfth house, there is a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.

If the lord of the seventh house is situated in an unfavorable house (duḥsthāna), and the fifth house is conjoined with the Moon, and the ascendant is joined by Saturn and Māndi, there is a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost. || 104 ||
If the lord of the eighth house is the son [Saturn], conjoined with Saturn and Venus,
and the significator (Kāraka) is situated in a sign of destruction, there is a loss of children due to the curse of a ghost.
To pacify this fault, one should perform a Śrāddha at Gayā;
one should also perform the Rudrābhiṣeka and cause the image of Brahmā to be given away.
O twice-born one, one should likewise give a cow, a silver vessel, and a sapphire;
thereafter, one should feed the Brahmins and bestow sacrificial fees upon them.
When this is done, the man’s release from the curse occurs;
the birth of a son takes place for him, and the increase of his lineage is brought about. || 108 ||

Likewise, O Brahmin, when there is a defect caused by Jupiter or Venus, the attainment of a son occurs through the worship of Śambhu; and when it is caused by Jupiter or the Moon, it occurs through mantras, yantras, medicines, and so forth.

The defect caused by Rāhu is removed by the giving away of a daughter in marriage; that caused by Sūrya (the Sun) by the chanting of Hari's names; that caused by Ketu by the gift of a cow; and those caused by Kuja (Mars) and Arkija (Saturn) by the recitation of the Rudra-mantras.
O twice-born one, for the destruction of all defects and for the attainment of an auspicious lineage, the story of the Harivaṃśa should be heard with devotion according to the prescribed rule.
Now begins the chapter on the pacification of planetary influences. || 84 ||
O Sage, for the sake of pacifying the afflictions of the planets and for the benefit of human beings, please describe the ritual procedure for their worship in brief out of compassion. (1)
O best of the twice-born, the planets beginning with the Sun were previously described by me;
the happiness and suffering of all living beings in this world are dependent upon them.
Therefore, one who desires great peace, or prosperity, or with a pure mind desires long life and nourishment, should perform their sacrifice. (3)
The planets should be fashioned in order from copper, crystal, red sandalwood,
gold, silver, iron, lead, and bell-metal.
Or they may be painted on a cloth by the best of the twice-born using their respective colors as previously described,
in their own assigned directions, or within decorative designs such as lotuses and the like.
The Sun-god has the lotus posture, holds a lotus in his hand, possesses a luster like that of a lotus petal,
is seated upon a chariot drawn by seven horses, and has two arms.
O twice-born one, the god should be fashioned as white, clad in white garments, possessing ten horses and white ornaments, two-armed, with a mace in his hand, and resembling the moon.
Wearing red garlands and garments, holding a spear, a trident, and a mace, the four-armed Maṅgala, who bestows boons, has a ram for his vehicle. || 8 ||
Wearing yellow garlands and garments, with a luster like that of the *karṇikāra* flower,
holding a sword, shield, and mace in his hands, the wise planet Mercury stands upon a lion and bestows boons.
Guru and Śukra should be depicted respectively as yellow and white in color, each with four arms,
holding a staff and granting boons, and carrying a rosary and a water-pot.
O twice-born one, the son of the Sun is to be known as having the luster of sapphire, bearing a trident, granting boons, riding upon a vulture, and holding an arrow and a bow.
With a terrifying face, holding a sword, shield, and trident, bestowing boons, seated upon a lion, and blue in color— thus is Rāhu envisioned.
All smoke-colored, two-armed, wielding maces, and having deformed faces, they shall always have vultures as their vehicles; such are the banners that bestow boons.
All the planets that bestow welfare upon the world should be made by the wise with crowns;
they should always be one hundred and eight in number and elevated by their own [respective] finger-breadths.
Fine garments should be offered according to their respective colors; likewise, perfume, a lamp, an oblation, and incense made of guggulu should be presented. 15.
Whatever substance is the food of a particular planet, and whatever is dear to it—
that should be offered to it with a mind imbued with devotion.
Then one should recite the mantra portions beginning with "ākṛṣṇena," "imaṃ devā," "agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakut," and "udbudhyasva," as well as those of Bṛhaspati. (17)
"From food [it is] distilled," and "May the divine waters come for our desire," and likewise "With what [splendor], O Wondrous One?"—thus making these the banners. (18)
The seven Rudras, the Nandas of the quarters, the nine moons, and likewise the kings;
the three fortnights, the eight moons, and similarly the seven moons. (19)

O best of the twice-born, these numbers, multiplied by one thousand, are proclaimed as the counts for recitation (japa) for the purpose of pleasing the planets beginning with the Sun, in their respective order.
Arka, palāśa, khadira, apāmārga, pippala, udumbara, śamī, dūrvā, and kuśa are the sacrificial fuels (samidh) in their respective order. || 21 ||
They should be offered with honey and clarified butter, or combined with curd or milk;
for each [deity], one hundred and eight or twenty-eight [oblations] are prescribed.
Rice with jaggery, milk-rice, sacrificial food, six-day rice with milk, curd-rice, sacrificial flour, meat, and variegated rice. || 23 ||
O twice-born one, one should thus give food to the Brahmins according to the sequence of the planets;
or, according to one's capacity and as available, it should be given with due honor.
A cow, a conch, likewise a bull, gold, a garment, a horse, in order; a black cow, iron, and a goat—these are the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) for the Sun and the other [planets]. || 25 ||
Whoever is in distress at whatever time should worship that [deity] with effort;
this boon was granted to them by the Creator: "When you are worshipped, you shall in turn worship. (26)
The prosperity and downfall of human beings, as well as the existence and non-existence of the worlds, are dependent upon the planets; therefore, the planets are most worthy of worship. (27)
Now begins the eighty-fifth chapter: On the Description of Inauspicious Births.
Now I shall further explain another matter: even when there is an auspicious lunar mansion and favorable planets, birth may become inauspicious due to other causes. || 1 ||

On the new moon day, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, during the Viṣṭi karana, under the Sodarā nakṣatra, under the Pitṛ nakṣatra, at the sun's transit (saṃkrānti), during the Pāta yoga, and likewise during solar and lunar eclipses; || 2 ||
In difficult yogas such as Vyatīpāta and others, in the three types of Gaṇḍānta,
in Yamaghaṇṭa, Avama, Dagdhayoga, and in the birth of a Triṣaṅkhyā (triple-junction), [these are unfavorable].
Even though there are three types of birth (prasava), it should be known that birth is inauspicious;
through pacification (śānti), it becomes auspicious, and I shall now state the means for that.
Now begins the chapter on the pacification of birth at the time of the new moon: Chapter 86.
O Maitreya, for those who have recently given birth, there may be poverty on the part of the parents;
to avoid that fault, a wise person should perform a rite of pacification. || 1 ||
Having first performed the ritual installation of the water-pot according to the prescribed rules,
one should likewise [place] the sprouts of the Udumbara, Plakṣa, Aśvattha, and Cūta trees.
One should place the roots and bark of the *nimba* trees there;
having cast in the five jewels, one should cover it with a pair of garments.
Having addressed the water-pot with the mantra "sarve samudrāḥ" and the three-verse hymn beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭhā," he should place it in the southeast corner.
Then, for the two deities of the new moon— the Moon and the Sun—
one should daily [worship] their images made respectively of gold, silver, and likewise copper.
Having propitiated Savitṛ with the mantra "āpyāyasva" and with the other [mantras] from the end,
and having honored him with the ritual services (upacāras), one should then perform the fire-oblation (homa).
The wise observer of the vow should offer the fuel-sticks and the sacrificial porridge (caru) in sequence with devotion,
using the Savitṛ mantra for the former and the Soma-dhenu mantra for the latter.
One should likewise perform the consecration (abhiṣeka) one hundred and eight times, or even twenty-eight times, for the couple and their virtuous sons.
Gold, silver, and a black cow shall be the sacrificial fee;
one should feed the Brahmins according to one's ability, and thereby obtain security.
Now begins the chapter on propitiatory rites for the birth [of a child] on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight. 87.

O twice-born one, the fruit [of the birth] in the six divisions of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight is as follows in sequence: if the birth occurs in the first division, then it should be known as auspicious. (1)
In the second [month] he kills his father, and in the third his mother;
in the fourth he kills his maternal uncle, and in the fifth there is the destruction of the lineage.
In the sixth [house], however, there shall be loss of wealth or even the destruction of oneself;
for the sake of averting that evil, one should diligently perform a propitiatory rite (śānti).
One should fashion an image of Śiva made of gold weighing one karṣa,
or even half of that, or a quarter, according to one's wealth, making it beautiful.
She wears a crown of crescent moons and is adorned with white garlands and garments;
she has three eyes, is seated upon a bull, and displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
The preceptor, who is a knower of the true nature of mantras, should perform the worship with the mantra "Tryambakam" without weariness, having invoked [the deity] with mantras dedicated to Varuṇa.
With the verse beginning "imaṃ me varuṇa," with the verse beginning "tattvā yāmi," again with the verse beginning "tvam naḥ agne," and also with the verse beginning "sa tvam naḥ. || 7 ||
Beginning with the pitcher dedicated to Agni, one should worship it in due order with devotion,
reciting the *sūkta* "ā no bhadrā" and the *sūkta* "bhadrā agneḥ."
Having recited the Puruṣasūkta and likewise the Kandrudra,
one should perform the consecration of Śaṅkara and the worship of the planets.
One should offer sacrificial fuel, clarified butter, cooked rice, sesame, mung beans, and mustard seeds; as well as auspicious sacrificial wood from the aśvattha, plakṣa, pālāśa, and khadira trees.
One should offer one hundred and eight oblations into the fire according to the prescribed rite,
or one may perform the homa separately with a count of twenty-eight for each.
Then, with the Tryambaka mantra and likewise with the Vyāhṛtis, one should perform the oblation to the planets according to the rules; from that, security shall arise.
The wise knower of mantras should then perform the consecration (abhiṣeka) for the newborn and for his parents;
thereafter, he should feed the Brahmins according to his capacity.
Now begins the eighty-eighth chapter: On the Pacification of Adverse Yogas.

Now I shall fully explain that which pertains to the Bhadrā and Avama muhūrtas, as well as to evil planetary configurations such as Vyātyupāta, and to the Yamaghaṇṭa and other such [inauspicious] conjunctions. || 1 ||
O twice-born one, the birth of such a child is said to yield inauspicious results;
therefore, when a difficult birth-configuration occurs, a wise man should perform the rite of pacification.
Or, when an auspicious lunar mansion and a favorable day have been indicated by astrologers, the householder should perform the worship of the deities as well as the sacrifice to the planets. (3)
One should perform the consecration of Śaṅkara, offer a lamp of ghee in the temple of Śiva, and perform circumambulation of the Aśvattha tree; these acts increase one's lifespan.
The wise man, having performed the oblation one hundred and eight times with the Viṣṇu-mantra, should feed the Brāhmaṇas according to his capacity; thereafter, he shall attain auspiciousness. || 5 ||
Now begins the chapter on the pacification of being born under a single lunar mansion (Ekanakṣatra). || 89 ||
Now, if the birth of two brothers, or of a father and son, occurs under the same lunar mansion, or if the death of one of them occurs at that very same time, this is the certainty. (1)
In this regard, I shall proclaim the rite of pacification as spoken by Garga and other sages:
on an auspicious day, under a favorable lunar mansion, and endowed with the strength of the moon and stars.

One should perform the rite of pacification (śānti) at an auspicious time, avoiding the empty asterisms (riktās) and the Viṣṭi yoga. In the northeast direction from the planet Śani, one should fashion an auspicious image of the asterism.
One should worship [the deity] upon the water-pot with the mantra prescribed for that constellation;
having covered it with a red cloth, one should encircle it with a pair of garments.
One should likewise perform the fire-offering (agnimukha) according to the path prescribed in one's own Vedic branch;
then, with that same mantra, one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times.
For each [deity], one should indeed perform the rites up to the expiation (prāyaścitta) with fuel-sticks, food, and clarified butter;
thereafter, the preceptor should perform the consecration (abhiṣeka) for both.
One should give sacrificial fees to the officiating priests, especially to the preceptor;
one should feed the Brahmins with devotion, free from stinginess regarding wealth.
Now begins the chapter on the pacification of [inauspicious] transits and births. || 90 ||
Ghorā, Adhvāṅkṣī, Mahodarī, Mandā, Mandākinī, as well as Miśrā and Rākṣasī; these [occur] from the sun's transit on a Sunday. || 1 ||
A man born at the moment of a solar transit (saṃkrānti) shall experience the suffering of poverty;
he attains happiness through propitiatory rites (śānti). Therefore, I shall now describe the procedure for that propitiation.
One should perform the sacrifice to the nine planets for the pacification of his afflictions,
having smeared the eastern part of the house with cow dung.
In a well-adorned place,
one should prepare a heap of grain measuring five *droṇas*, and likewise half that amount of husked rice.
O best of the twice-born, one should then make a heap of sesame seeds half that size;
and upon each of these three separate heaps, wise men should draw an eight-petaled lotus.
Having caused the proclamation of an auspicious day, one should first choose a preceptor who knows the Dharma, understands the true nature of mantras, and is skilled in rites for pacification.
One should place unblemished and very beautiful jars upon the astrological signs (rāśis),
filling them with water from sacred fords (tīrtha) along with medicinal herbs and sprouts.
One should pour the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) into that [vessel], wrap it with a pair of cloths,
and place a vessel covered with a fine cloth upon the water-pot.
One should install there an image together with its presiding deity (adhidevatā) and counter-deity (pratyadhidaivata); the Sun shall be the presiding deity, and the Moon the counter-deity.
One should worship the Saṃkrānti in the center, with the forms of the Moon and Sun on either side;
prior to the worship of the image, one should offer a pair of garments.
Then one should worship with the respective mantra preceded by the *vyāhṛtis*;
one should worship the primary image with the *traiyambaka* mantra.
One should perform the worship of the Sun with the mantra "utsūrya," and one should perform the worship of the Moon with the mantra "āpyāyasva. || 12 ||
Touching the principal image while reciting the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, using either the sixteen services or the five services.
One should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times, or one hundred and eight times;
or else, according to one's capacity, one may recite it twenty-eight times.
To the west of the water-jars, one should prepare the fire upon a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila);
one should cause the consecrated fire to be established according to the procedure prescribed in one's own Gṛhya-sūtra.
One should offer fuel-sticks, clarified butter, and sacrificial porridge with the *trayambaka* mantra,
either one thousand and eight times or one hundred and eight times, as appropriate.
One should perform exactly twenty-eight oblations according to one's capacity;
one should also have the oblation of sesame seeds performed with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra.
Then, having offered the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation, one should perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*);
afterwards, one should feed the Brahmins; in this way, one shall attain peace. || 18 ||
The End of India
